topics.quote: no you dont, i signed up without one
topics.summary: An Indian applicant believes a referral is needed to get access or projects, and one commenter agrees, while others say you can sign up without one and just have to wait for a project.

topics.quote: Doesn't work like that. You just have to wait for a project
topics.summary: Getting projects after joining is described as a matter of waiting until one is assigned.

topics.quote: Ai and data workers exploited- they get rich while you chase tasks
topics.summary: The post shares a video claiming AI data workers are exploited while the companies get rich, and a commenter agrees.

topics.quote: Contrary to popular belief around here, they are doing human reviews. They can see when people are grinding the clock.
topics.summary: The poster notes frequent complaints about offboarding for quality issues, while a commenter says reviews are done by humans who can tell honest mistakes from bad work, though their own mistakes got them moved back to the generalist pool.

topics.quote: There's no way to maximize earnings other than working while you can.
topics.summary: Generalist Aether work pays a flat rate, so the only way to earn more is to work more hours.

topics.quote: Too many mistakes piled up. So they put me back in the generalist pool. At least I didn't get booted altogether.
topics.summary: People are often offboarded for quality issues, and one commenter was dropped from better tasks back to the generalist pool after making mistakes.

topics.quote: You clock in and work until the hours are up for the day.
topics.summary: Generalist work has a daily hour limit, and workers clock in until they reach it.

topics.quote: is anyone else getting slow load times and now I am getting gateway time out constantly.
topics.summary: Several workers report the Outlier site loading slowly, hanging and giving gateway timeouts so they cannot continue tasking.

topics.quote: My Outlier account was permanently deactivated earlier this year due to alleged policy violations.
topics.summary: The poster's account was permanently deactivated for alleged policy violations without a clear explanation, and commenters say there is no chance of reversal because Outlier can remove people for any reason.

topics.quote: I did this to obtain more information about an alleged violation, but they haven't responded yet.
topics.summary: Support upheld the ban after two reviews without explaining what triggered it, and a commenter's GDPR data request had gone unanswered for most of the 30-day legal deadline.

topics.quote: i guess u has been removed from project. It still appear
topics.summary: A commenter suggests the poster was likely removed from the project without notice, since the task still appears for others.

topics.quote: I just logged in and noticed the video comparison task disappeared.
topics.summary: The poster found that the video comparison task they had been working on was suddenly gone from their dashboard.

topics.quote: I had Oracle status, was doing well, and had a good rating. I always tried to follow the rules and submit good work, but my account was suddenly removed without a clear reason.
topics.summary: Many workers, including high-rated Oracles, report sudden deactivation without explanation, though some say accounts are often restored later.

topics.quote: They also have witheld my earnings from last week.
topics.summary: Deactivated workers report their pending earnings were withheld or unpaid, with one saying they have not been paid for months.

topics.quote: No reason has been given and I keep getting the same bot reply, and pending payment has been unpaid.
topics.summary: Support gives bot replies and does not address the mass deactivations; an escalation form and a Reddit staff DM offer are the only routes to a human, which commenters find inadequate.

topics.quote: The task time was only 7 minutes, but that was not enough for many tasks because the image requirements only showed after opening the task.
topics.summary: The poster says the 7-minute task limit on Pixel Smith was too short, so their average was about 9 minutes.

topics.quote: It's always to do with their budgets, I have been fired and rehired with a close to perfect ranking 3 times in 4 months.
topics.summary: One commenter says removals are budget-driven, and they have been dropped and rehired three times in four months.

topics.quote: I successfully passed the screening for the Aether Project, but it's been 3 days and still no tasks.
topics.summary: The poster has had no tasks for three days after passing screening, and a commenter says most projects are in an empty-queue state except the Live S2S Elo task.

topics.quote: Although from my earnings, it shows that I already completed a couple of task though no duration was recorded, nor were any earnings.
topics.summary: A new worker reports that the time tracker stayed at zero or showed 'Idle activity detected' even with screen sharing on, so completed tasks recorded no time and no earnings.

topics.quote: It was just a dollar
topics.summary: The poster says the assessments paid only a tiny amount, about one dollar.

topics.quote: Has anyone had their Outlier account deactivated after an account review?
topics.summary: The poster asks whether others have had their Outlier account deactivated after an account review. The body was removed, so no details remain.

topics.quote: Blacklisted
topics.summary: The poster says they were blacklisted by Outlier and would never recommend working there.

topics.quote: however the project ended and wrapped up, now there's been nothing in the market for several days
topics.summary: A new worker did 7 tasks before their first project ended, has seen no work for several days, and is asking how often new projects appear; a commenter points to a pinned announcement about project availability.

topics.quote: my account was suddenly deactivated just hours after I passed the LATAM Coder assessment
topics.summary: The poster says their account was deactivated without explanation hours after passing a coding assessment, despite following the rules.

topics.quote: If you manage to get an human from support, you might have a chance. But it's tough, have been trying for longer than a month and nothing.
topics.summary: Commenters point the poster to support, and one says they have tried for over a month without reaching a human.

topics.quote: Got a notice I failed the generalist skill screening (for expert capability in English).
topics.summary: A highly credentialed applicant failed the English skill screening while passing the law one, and others call the screenings nitpicky, though a retake is usually allowed after 14 days.

topics.quote: Was just blankly told the results are final. Not even a check to see if it was a substantive result as opposed to a technical issue.
topics.summary: Support refused to check whether the failed screening was a technical glitch and simply said results are final.

topics.quote: I advise you to stay away from this company, their system has gone downhill since the end of 2024
topics.summary: One commenter advises staying away from the company, saying its system has declined since late 2024.

topics.quote: My Outlier account was suddenly deactivated while I was taking the Aether screening test. The reason given was related to a copy/paste issue.
topics.summary: A contributor with a 4+ rating was deactivated during a screening for pasting their own transcription from Notepad, and a commenter says copy/paste is banned with no nuance.

topics.quote: What is frustrating is that my account was deactivated without, as far as I understand, anyone actually reviewing the context of what happened.
topics.summary: The poster feels no human reviewed the context and asks whether an appeal is possible, while a commenter doubts Outlier has the resources to check individual cases.

topics.quote: The text box provided for the transcription was extremely small, which made it difficult for me to work comfortably.
topics.summary: The screening's transcription text box was too small to work in comfortably.

topics.quote: I also failed and got the same email. No webinar anywhere for me as well.
topics.summary: People failed the Aether onboarding, which they found subjectively graded, and were promised a second-chance webinar that they cannot find.

topics.quote: I feel like it’s an automated email and maybe there was a webinar at some point but isn’t there anymore so seems like it’s straight up lying now.
topics.summary: One person says AI chat support tickets usually get answered in a day or two, while others got no email, or a dismissive "it happens," or an automated email that seems misleading.

topics.quote: I was just banned from Outlier after 7/8 days working ONLY with Aether.
topics.summary: One worker reports being banned after about a week of working only on Aether and advises looking for other projects.

topics.quote: Finally I've got the project after 3 month
topics.summary: The poster says they finally got a project after waiting three months.

topics.quote: start looking for a new gig as no matter what you do once they have enough they seem to kick people out no matter the score or rating.
topics.summary: Several people describe being kicked from Aether or suspended from Outlier, often for no clear reason, and the opening poster later says his own account was suspended after a week.

topics.quote: Oh my bad, like you should stop the timers if you stop working.
topics.summary: Commenters warn against staying idle during tasks or leaving timers running, but say that taking days off between tasks has caused them no problems.

topics.quote: I never had issues with payment in the month I was in, maybe came a day late but you will be payed.
topics.summary: One worker says pay arrived reliably, at most a day late.

topics.quote: I received many kind and good feedbacks, but I have to understand more about their criterias.
topics.summary: The opening poster reports a 4.35 average with mostly 5/5 scores and some low ones, and a commenter says high scores do not protect you from removal.

topics.quote: It has been three days since I created my account, but I haven't been added to the Aether project; no projects are visible.
topics.summary: Some people say they see no projects at all, or have had no new work since being dropped from Aether.

topics.quote: That’s not so easy to deal with, because there’s no contract.
topics.summary: Workers mention the anxiety of having no contract and note that screens are recorded while working.

topics.quote: I made the screening/assessment and passed it, but had to wait some days to start since I’m having some problems with my PC’s screen.
topics.summary: The opening poster passed the screening, and another commenter says Aether requires its own specific assessment.

topics.quote: I have finished HoneyBee SXS's onboarding and have no idea what to do in my first task.
topics.summary: Honeybee tasks are described as complex, confusing and stressful but less repetitive and educational, while Aether micro tasks are easy, flexible and sometimes tedious.

topics.quote: For my case, pay for Aether is much better than Honeybee SXS, the pay for honeybee doesn't really worth the amount of work that you have to do.
topics.summary: Honeybee reportedly pays about twice Aether per hour in some places and had high-paying missions, but others say the pay is not worth the effort or differs by country.

topics.quote: I was working for like 4 hours, I didn't meet the due time. All for nothing.
topics.summary: Honeybee tasks take 2 to 6 hours each, and workers who missed the deadline lost hours of unpaid work.

topics.quote: kind of sucks though as it won’t let me do any tasks on Aether until I’ve onboarded with Honeybee. Totally locked it off for me.
topics.summary: Project priority settings block workers from their current project until they onboard or leave, tasks disappear, and Honeybee has had empty queues with people shuffled around.

topics.quote: I've seen reviews on reddit and elsewhere abt the problems with honeybee onboarding and random platform bans for no fault of people.
topics.summary: People worry about reports of random platform bans tied to Honeybee onboarding and random removals from Aether, but nobody reports this happening to them.

topics.quote: They just added a requirement to buy your own Pro accounts to keep tasking on SxS. $399 per month.
topics.summary: A new requirement for workers to buy $399-per-month Pro accounts to keep working on Honeybee led at least one person to leave.

topics.quote: Tasking on Honeybee for more than a month now, most amazing team there is a war room you can ask help anytime.
topics.summary: Honeybee has a 24-hour war room where quality managers answer questions, though the many new joiners mean lots of repeated questions.

topics.quote: They took me off Aether even though I had a 4.0 score. I can still access the website
topics.summary: Workers on the Aether project report being deactivated or dropped from the project despite good scores, and the appeal was denied with a claim of dishonest behavior.

topics.quote: This matter has been reviewed, and the deactivation stands.
topics.summary: Support tickets and the bot gave little explanation, and a staff reply upheld the deactivation with a generic Terms of Use violation.

topics.quote: My scores are 4.33/5 and 90/100 but it seems as if they don't consider it....
topics.summary: High quality scores did not protect workers, and an AI-led interview after an account review led to removal.

topics.quote: Ineligible for Aether like many others recently today and wondering about options
topics.summary: The poster says they and many others were recently made ineligible for the Aether project and asks what options they have.

topics.quote: Haven't seen any since June.
topics.summary: The poster has seen no coding projects since June, and a commenter who used to do coding work suggests such work has dried up because models rarely make mistakes now.

topics.quote: I was informed that the decision was final following a secondary human review, but I was never told what specific activity or violation led to the deactivation.
topics.summary: The poster's account was permanently deactivated during onboarding for a new project with no specific reason given, and appeals were rejected.

topics.quote: Unfortunately, all my requests were rejected.
topics.summary: Support rejected the appeal and reinstatement request, and the company's reply cited only unspecified Terms of Use violations, pointing back to Support.

topics.quote: DataAnnotation tasks disappearing after submission — anyone else facing this?
topics.summary: The poster asks whether others also see their DataAnnotation tasks disappear after they submit them; the post body was removed.

topics.quote: Dash was then dry for a day and a half till it fully populated. Keep in mind there is a dry spell going on right now so even people who've been on DA for a while are low in tasks.
topics.summary: A new worker has had no projects for two days after finishing qualifications; others say it takes a few days, that there is currently a dry spell even for veterans, and that tasks are first come first serve.

topics.quote: I did the application and got accepted instantly. I then did the core assessment and that also got accepted instantly.
topics.summary: Commenters explain that new workers' qualification work is checked or audited before projects appear, and the timing varies by person and region.

topics.quote: Report time only shows the submitted projects in the last 24 hours
topics.summary: Commenters ask whether time was reported for qualification tasks, and the poster notes the report-time tab only shows submissions from the last 24 hours.

topics.quote: You are paid $45/hr to take the qualification. In my experience most of the finance/accounting work pays $50-$60/hr, occasionally higher.
topics.summary: The accounting qualification pays $45/hr, and one worker says most finance and accounting work pays $50-$60/hr, sometimes more.

topics.quote: I have not yet seen any projects or heard back yet. It’s been 2 weeks since I completed the accounting and probably 5 days since the finance.
topics.summary: Passing a qualification is not officially announced. Some workers saw projects appear on their dashboard within days, while others heard nothing for weeks.

topics.quote: In my experience the qualifications tend to require time on the higher end of what they estimate but I typically work carefully on the quals to make sure I do a good job.
topics.summary: Qualifications often take as long as the top of the time estimate or longer, and workers are unsure whether going over matters.

topics.quote: I never actually got an official notification but projects started showing up on my dash.
topics.summary: Workers get no official message about qualification results and have to infer them from projects showing up.

topics.quote: Yay I just refreshed the webpage and I got approved! Just got my ID approved so can start working now!
topics.summary: The poster passed the starter assessment, then the seven qualifications and ID verification, and was approved quickly; another worker was confused because their assessments came before the starter guide.

topics.quote: Been doing this over a year and this is the first time I’ve never not had work for this long.
topics.summary: Several established workers report a drought with zero tasks and zero qualifications for days, while the newly approved poster was given one 12-task starter project.

topics.quote: It’s assessing the AI response against a rubric which is easy but quite boring.
topics.summary: The first project is rating AI responses against a rubric, which the poster finds easy but boring.

topics.quote: Yeah there’s 1 project available containing 12 tasks at $25/hr.
topics.summary: The starter project pays $25 an hour.

topics.quote: Project not found on da$hboard after completing a$$esment.
topics.summary: The poster finished a project assessment but the project did not appear on their dashboard, and they asked why.

topics.quote: Anyone got projects or any response after doing Agentic Qual
topics.summary: The poster asks whether anyone got projects or heard back after completing the Agentic qualification.

topics.quote: So I didn't pass?
topics.summary: The poster asks whether they failed the DataAnnotation assessment, but the body of the post was removed.

topics.quote: I just use my phone, I only work on my laptop, but to check for tasks, trigger payouts I do on my phone wherever I am.
topics.summary: The poster asks whether remotely accessing their desktop from a phone to check for tasks is allowed, and a commenter says they simply check tasks and trigger payouts from their phone but do the actual work on a laptop.

topics.quote: Suggested qualification isn't showing up?
topics.summary: The poster asks why a suggested qualification is not appearing for them; the post body was removed.

topics.quote: Did anyone else lose "the project"
topics.summary: The poster asks whether others also lost access to a particular project; the post body was removed.

topics.quote: Any advice for someone who's been waiting over 2 months without getting a single project?
topics.summary: Some people have earned well, while others report waiting months with no projects or getting no tasks after a small first earning.

topics.quote: Just hit my first $1,000 on DataAnnotation.
topics.summary: The poster and a commenter each report reaching $1,000 in earnings on DataAnnotation.

topics.quote: Fill out your profile (add skills), take qualifications if they appear.
topics.summary: Commenters advise filling out skills and taking qualifications, and one says most of their earnings came from paid quals and trainings.

topics.quote: Core work is only available in the core countries: US, Canada, Ireland, UK, Australia, and New Zealand.
topics.summary: A bilingual worker gets only sparse bilingual jobs despite passing core and STEM quals; others say core work is limited to certain countries, though some bilingual workers did get coding projects.

topics.quote: I completed the maths one pretty well (IMO) but didn’t hear anything since…hope it’s not over
topics.summary: People describe taking many qualification tests, with some hearing nothing back after them and others being let into coding projects; one person asks how long acceptance takes after the first interview.

topics.quote: Just got some coding projects, but they all seem to be orders of magnitude above the quals
topics.summary: One worker says the coding projects they received are much harder than the qualification tests suggested.

topics.quote: Anyways I just uploaded the test, wish me luck!
topics.summary: The poster just submitted the DataAnnotation starter test, asks whether their source citation format matters, and asks if anyone got in recently.

topics.quote: Don't post confidential material here.
topics.summary: A commenter warns that test content is covered by an NDA and should not be shared publicly.

topics.quote: Human feedback is very rare and random on DA.
topics.summary: People disagree on whether DataAnnotation gives feedback on submitted work: one says human feedback is rare and random, another says feedback is given only for minor fixable mistakes.

topics.quote: Having access to projects is the best, and sometimes only, feedback.
topics.summary: Workers can't easily tell whether they have been dropped from a project, and still having project access is the main sign of standing.

topics.quote: Submitted
topics.summary: The poster says only that they submitted something, most likely their application or assessment, with no outcome given.

topics.quote: Indian bilinguals, did anyone got the university course?
topics.summary: Indian bilingual workers ask whether others received a specific project with 'university' in its name, and one says yes.

topics.quote: Why no projects are coming!
topics.summary: The poster complains that no projects are showing up for them.

topics.quote: Most, if not all, creation projects need American English.
topics.summary: The poster notes that most creation projects require American English and asks how to make Copilot write in American spelling from outside the US.

topics.quote: That you cannot change your paypal email. And you should be extremely careful about it
topics.summary: Commenters say DataAnnotation does not let workers change their PayPal email, and the onboarding warns about this repeatedly.

topics.quote: He didn't have much projects since 4 months just one or 2 small basic projects which paid 18$/ hour and he just had 438$ since 4 months
topics.summary: A friend reportedly had only one or two small projects in four months and earned $438.

topics.quote: He didn't have much projects since 4 months just one or 2 small basic projects which paid 18$/ hour and he just had 438$ since 4 months
topics.summary: Basic generalist projects reportedly paid $18/hour, and one commenter says the platform can pay $13k a year.

topics.quote: It won't show up in your Report Time section unless you submit a task.
topics.summary: Time spent on a task that is skipped or abandoned without submitting cannot be logged, so workers lose it unpaid unless the project explicitly provides an escape hatch.

topics.quote: And people wonder why they get DOD
topics.summary: One commenter suggests that logging time for unsubmitted work is the kind of thing that gets accounts deactivated.

topics.quote: Since then, no more coding projects showed up, only generalists and STEM.
topics.summary: The poster had steady coding work for months, then coding projects stopped appearing. Others guess that qualifications rotate or that people mostly get work in the category they started in.

topics.quote: Or did I just get dropped from coding projects at all?
topics.summary: The poster wonders whether they were quietly dropped from coding projects without being told.

topics.quote: someone told me that quals are rotational and will again show up, so we can re-qualify for coding projects.
topics.summary: People discuss passing the coding assessment, re-qualifying through rotating qualification tests, and possible location or background check requirements for projects.

topics.quote: I have lost access to my Mercor account tried everything, can i make a different account using a different email id?
topics.summary: The poster lost access to their Mercor account and asks whether they can make a new one with another email, and a commenter simply says no.

topics.quote: Usually during the night
topics.summary: A new worker asks when Mercor moves payments from pending to processed, and a commenter says it usually happens overnight.

topics.quote: I was unsuccessful in taking this interview a few months ago and I really wanna pass it this time and it was a lot harder than anticipated.
topics.summary: The poster failed Mercor's domain expert interview, found it harder than expected, and is asking for tips and resources before retrying.

topics.quote: Does Mercor give job offers to Africans (especially west africa)
topics.summary: The poster asks whether Mercor accepts applicants from Africa, especially West Africa; the post body was removed and there are no answers.

topics.quote: For me at least they usually show back up, sometimes after a few days sometimes weeks, sometimes I get mail on them and then there are no more tasks when I try and do one :(
topics.summary: Many workers saw projects vanish from their dashboard after submitting long coding tasks; some report the projects came back within hours or days, while others are still waiting.

topics.quote: the task also got expired by 1 minute due to checks which took approx 10 mins 😭, and now I am worried..
topics.summary: Workers describe long task timers of 8-20 hours, tasks expiring during checks, and a possible lockout period of about 24 hours after a big submission.

topics.quote: I also got my first feedback today and it was very positive so I'm quite happy about that
topics.summary: Some workers suspect automatic quality holds after submission, and one reports getting positive feedback.

topics.quote: Nope. Shit just happens.
topics.summary: Project disappearances are not explained, workers don't contact support about them, and one project returned with an unannounced instruction update.

topics.quote: It was 11 hours, also used escape hatch because the model just cannot fail.
topics.summary: The coding tasks are long, high-paying, and require making the model fail, which workers find hard.

topics.quote: Oh, a project for the most boring people in your life!
topics.summary: The poster mocks a Mercor project listing as being for very boring people, suggesting the work looks tedious.

topics.quote: I don't remember it being particularly hard.
topics.summary: The final registration step is a 15-minute AI video interview based on your CV that asks about past roles and skills, and one commenter recalls it being easy.

topics.quote: From January 5 to March 30th I applied to 22 roles and got rejected from all of them. Gave up and stopped checking for roles to apply to.
topics.summary: Many people report dozens of rejections from applications and say the real way in is an unexpected instant offer months later, though a few were hired directly after applying and one had an instant offer cancelled during onboarding.

topics.quote: I did get lucky with my first contract, but it’s a stop/start sprint type, so I am hoping it just holds me over until I get that first instant offer
topics.summary: Some say their project has been steady since starting, while others describe paused or stop-start projects and no new contracts for months.

topics.quote: If they say you are a great match and you applied. Then there is a 99% chance that they will offer the contract within 1-3 days.
topics.summary: People invited to apply for an AI safety red teaming project are waiting without an offer. One commenter says an invite usually leads to a contract within 1-3 days.

topics.quote: But I haven't been acep6in anything, does having a Mexican Id affects the process?
topics.summary: A Mexico-based applicant with a forestry master's and a biology PhD has applied to many projects without being accepted and asks whether a Mexican ID affects the process.

topics.quote: Assessments are validated, but the results are not announced.
topics.summary: People who finished Mercor assessments ask how long validation takes and are told results are never announced, which leaves them unsure whether they can apply to jobs.

topics.quote: I went through about a month with no offers after it ended and then landed up with 2 contracts
topics.summary: Project lengths vary widely, from a couple of days to over 8 months, and some run longer than planned, but projects pause or end and there can be gaps of a month with no offers.

topics.quote: Hours fluctuated but it pulled in steady amounts and paid very well.
topics.summary: One worker said their 8-month project paid very well.

topics.quote: there was lots of revisions and reviews and the tasks were lengthy, things had to be perfect.
topics.summary: One long project involved lengthy expert-domain tasks with many revisions and high quality demands.

topics.quote: hone in your strongest areas especially in your profile, apply for relevant positions or generalist ones and keep checking newest posts and apply.
topics.summary: Advice to get new projects is to strengthen your profile and keep applying to new postings.

topics.quote: Unofficial communication channels and IRL groups are usually not a good idea, because NDAs get thrown into the trash as soon as people get together, and someone will eventually snitch.
topics.summary: A commenter warns that meeting other workers risks breaking NDAs. Their own bad experience was on a different platform, not Mercor.

topics.quote: Seeing that this can feel horribly isolating I was wondering if anyone might want to meet up sometime.
topics.summary: A part-time Mercor worker says the work can feel very isolating and suggests an in-person meetup.

topics.quote: coming over from HAI, got my first offer from mercor.
topics.summary: The poster and a commenter received contract offers for a video contributor project, and another asked where to find the onboarding form.

topics.quote: Just understand the risks associated with a task-based payment structure so you don't end up doing free work.
topics.summary: The offer pays $10 per task, and a commenter warns that per-task pay can mean unpaid work, though it may still be worthwhile for people in countries with weaker currencies.

topics.quote: I think its Egocentric Household chores Video Contributer for $10-14/hr
topics.summary: The project involves recording first-person videos of household chores.

topics.quote: Not able to view mercor tasks in Google Drive
topics.summary: The poster says they cannot view their Mercor tasks in Google Drive.

topics.quote: Please escalate this to your project support in Slack.
topics.summary: A commenter points the poster to project support in Slack.

topics.quote: I have 15 years of experience in my field and all of my applications related to this field have been rejected.
topics.summary: Many experienced experts report being rejected for roles matching their expertise with no reason given, describe selection as random, and say offers mostly come via instant offers or after many repeated applications.

topics.quote: I too have more experience than some of these reviewers have been alive who make subjective guess at your work and send it back for a re-work.
topics.summary: One commenter complains that young, less experienced reviewers give subjective feedback and send work back for rework.

topics.quote: That's why I feel they need to tell us the reason for the rejection.
topics.summary: Commenters complain that Mercor gives no reason for rejections.

topics.quote: Some projects just never happen. They fail to collect enough workers or the client changes their mind, so the project is cancelled and everyone who applied gets rejected formally.
topics.summary: Some projects get cancelled or listings stay up after positions are filled, which leads to applicants being rejected.

topics.quote: Offers need to include more specifics and pre screen BEFORE someone accepts and onboards.
topics.summary: An 'instant work offer' required full onboarding and verification before revealing it was a one-time survey the worker didn't qualify for, and another got an offer unrelated to their profile.

topics.quote: I do not think they know what they are doing at all lol
topics.summary: Communication is seen as disorganized: details came only after onboarding with advice to let the contract expire, and one user got survey emails after being offboarded.

topics.quote: Also not impressed either the extremely invasive insightful tool.
topics.summary: A commenter complained that the Insightful monitoring tool is extremely invasive.

topics.quote: Got an offer email but no offer on the platform. Confused!
topics.summary: People told they qualified for a project and to expect a contract say they have heard nothing further and see no offer on the platform.

topics.quote: I got a email emailing I qualified for project Thor and to expect a email with my contract soon but I haven’t heard anything, anyone else dealing with this?
topics.summary: Workers are left without follow-up communication after being told a contract was coming.

topics.quote: I also got kicked off with little to no explanation.
topics.summary: Several workers say they were removed from projects without a clear reason, possibly in a mass offboarding, though some later got new offers.

topics.quote: Things were breaking and apps weren't working. I had a task that was stuck and wouldn't let me take any others.
topics.summary: The project had broken tools and stuck tasks before it was reset, and people discussed which browsers are safe to use with the tracking timer.

topics.quote: They opened alot of roles recently.
topics.summary: Some removed workers got new offers and new roles are opening, while others are still waiting for new offers.

topics.quote: I applied and did the AI interview. It was not nearly as difficult as I had myself worked up to think it was.
topics.summary: One applicant found the AI interview easier than expected, and others advise to keep applying and doing the assessments.

topics.quote: the insightful timer reports which apps you're spending time using
topics.summary: The Insightful time tracker records which apps workers use, so commenters suggest keeping a low profile with a common browser.

topics.quote: $50-70 an hour. Have to have a Bachelor's Degree and be in the US or Canada.

topics.summary: People report getting offers after onboarding, but some face further waiting while their contract is reviewed before they get access.

topics.quote: I am getting no help from the project leads.
topics.summary: Project leads gave no help or clear answers about the account status, and the only advice one person got was to post in Slack and keep logging on each day.

topics.quote: Hope to get a new instant offer soon for a new end client
topics.summary: After being offboarded, one worker is waiting for a new project offer.

topics.quote: I got 'Minor issues' then 'Major issues', that's why I'm gone today too?
topics.summary: Some link offboarding to 'Major issues' reviews or poor quality, while others say they had all tasks signed off or great reviews and were still dropped.

topics.quote: Just keep submitting for new projects and don’t count on longevity.
topics.summary: Commenters say projects rotate workers, onboard more people than needed, and change with client needs, so work is short-lived and not guaranteed.

topics.quote: Obviously, they won't explain why.

topics.quote: I started out at 40/hr as trial, then 55/hr at production, now im at 75/hr as super writer.
topics.summary: The offer was $60/hr, and one worker reports going from $40/hr in the trial to $55/hr in production and $75/hr as a Super Writer.

topics.summary: People are said to be offboarded often for quality issues, and one commenter was demoted from better tasks back to the generalist pool.

topics.quote: It was just a dollar

topics.summary: One commenter says support tickets usually get answered in a day or two, while others say the email promised a webinar that doesn't exist or got only a dismissive reply.

topics.summary: Honeybee reportedly pays about twice Aether's rate for some, but others outside the US find it not worth the effort, and rates seem to differ by country.

topics.summary: A long project involved lengthy expert-domain tasks with many revisions and high quality demands.

topics.quote: But I haven't been acep6in anything, does having a Mexican Id affects the process?
topics.summary: A highly qualified applicant in Mexico has applied to many biology and environment projects without being accepted and wonders whether a Mexican ID is the reason.

topics.quote: Assessments are validated, but the results are not announced.
topics.summary: People ask how long assessment validation takes, and one replies that results are never announced, which leaves applicants unsure whether they passed.

topics.quote: Seeing that this can feel horribly isolating I was wondering if anyone might want to meet up sometime.
topics.summary: The poster, who works part time for Mercor, says the work can feel very isolating.

topics.quote: Unofficial communication channels and IRL groups are usually not a good idea, because NDAs get thrown into the trash as soon as people get together, and someone will eventually snitch.
topics.summary: A commenter warns that worker meetups risk breaking NDAs, though their own bad experience was on another platform.

topics.quote: coming over from HAI, got my first offer from mercor.
topics.summary: The poster and a commenter received offers for a video contributor project, and another asks where to find the required onboarding form.

topics.quote: Just understand the risks associated with a task-based payment structure so you don't end up doing free work.
topics.summary: The offer pays $10 per task, and commenters weigh whether it is worth it, warning that per-task pay can mean unpaid work unless the local currency makes it worthwhile.

topics.quote: I think it’s just all random. I have 15 years of experience in my field and all of my applications related to this field have been rejected.
topics.summary: Many experienced experts report being rejected for roles matching their expertise without explanation, with selection seen as random or volume-driven; some get in via instant offers or after many applications.

topics.quote: I too have more experience than some of these reviewers have been alive who make subjective guess at your work and send it back for a re-work.
topics.summary: One worker complains that young, less experienced reviewers make subjective judgments and send work back.

topics.quote: Some projects just never happen. They fail to collect enough workers or the client changes their mind, so the project is cancelled and everyone who applied gets rejected formally.
topics.summary: A commenter explains that some projects get cancelled or listings stay up after filling, leading to rejections.

topics.quote: Not able to view mercor tasks in Google Drive
topics.summary: The poster says they cannot view their Mercor tasks in Google Drive, an access or tool problem.

topics.quote: Please escalate this to your project support in Slack.
topics.summary: A commenter suggests taking the problem to project support in Slack.

topics.quote: International student on F1 Status
topics.summary: The removed post's title asks about working for Mercor as an international student on an F1 visa, a question of legal eligibility to work as a contractor.

topics.quote: Same situation for me! Got an offer email but no offer on the platform. Confused!
topics.summary: People were told they qualified for a project and would get a contract, but nothing followed and no offer appeared on the platform.

topics.quote:
I also got kicked out today.  
The issue is that there is no way to get the correct reason.
topics.summary: The poster and several commenters were removed from projects after a few weeks with little or no explanation, and some think whole groups were cut regardless of quality.

topics.quote: Goodnews is I got another offer today and we back but wiser.
topics.summary: Some removed workers quickly got new offers and many roles are opening, while others have had no new offers yet.

topics.quote: Things were breaking and apps weren't working.
topics.summary: One project had broken tools and stuck tasks that could not be fixed, and people debated whether the time-tracker flags unusual browsers.

topics.quote: $50-70 an hour.
topics.summary: A recruiting email offered $50-70 an hour to US or Canadian applicants with a bachelor's degree.

topics.quote: I applied and did the AI interview. It was not nearly as difficult as I had myself worked up to think it was.
topics.summary: One applicant found the AI interview easier than expected.

topics.quote: They reimbursed us for that on my project within a couple of days once you upload the receipt.
topics.summary: One worker complained about having to pay for required programs, and another said those costs were reimbursed within days.

topics.quote: Offers need to include more specifics and pre screen BEFORE someone accepts and onboards.
topics.summary: The poster accepted an instant work offer and completed verifications and forms, then learned it was a one-time survey they did not qualify for. A commenter also got an offer unrelated to their profile.

topics.quote: I do not think they know what they are doing at all lol
topics.summary: Users describe poor communication: project details came only after onboarding, and one person was sent survey emails after being offboarded.

topics.quote: It’s a one time survey.
topics.summary: The instant offer turned out to be a single survey rather than ongoing work, possibly sent to the poster by mistake.

topics.quote: Yes you'll get access to everything eventually. I'm waiting for access to a few things as well.
topics.summary: A new worker confused by onboarding steps and logins is told access arrives eventually and that the onboarding documents answer most questions.

topics.quote: Make sure you have access to the timing app before reading the guide so you can get paid for it.
topics.summary: Commenters say time spent reading onboarding documents is paid if tracked in the timing app.

topics.quote: Any idea when the 40k person project will end
topics.summary: The poster asks when a large project with about 40,000 workers will end.

topics.quote: I have applied to 21 jobs so far, 2 submitted rn and the others rejected.
topics.summary: The poster has had most of 21 applications rejected within a couple of weeks, and one application has been pending for a month without a decision.

topics.quote: I did almost 50 tasks, and they didn't even mention why I was offboarded. It was my only income.
topics.summary: Many workers report being suddenly offboarded from a project after days or weeks without explanation, even with good reviews, though the email says it is not about performance.

topics.quote: Just keep submitting for new projects and don't count on longevity.
topics.summary: Projects rotate workers and task volume fluctuates, so work is short-lived and people must keep looking for the next project.

topics.quote: I got 'Minor issues' then 'Major issues', that's why I'm gone today too?
topics.summary: Some tie offboarding to bad review scores, while others say all their tasks were signed off with no issues and they were dropped anyway.

topics.quote: Obviously, they won't explain why.
topics.summary: Mercor sends a stock release email and gives no specific explanation for offboarding.

topics.quote: When I joined a project it said 8 hours but when my first task was accepted my hours were changed to 40
topics.summary: The poster got an offer capped at 6 hours a week, and several commenters say low caps are common during onboarding and are usually raised once the first tasks are reviewed and accepted.

topics.quote: I just completed the onboarding for my first offer. They're saying my contract is being reviewed. I thought I'd get direct access after signing that contract. I'm bummed
topics.summary: Some people received offers, sometimes instantly, while another finished onboarding and was disappointed to still be waiting on a contract review.

topics.quote: Is just a start but you can get more hours and likely to have more project .
topics.summary: One commenter expects more hours and more projects to follow after the initial start.

topics.quote: After 1 month on a project, my Feather account was suddenly put in Pending Reactivation status and I no longer have access to Feather.
topics.summary: The poster lost project access to a 'Pending Reactivation' status for a month without explanation. One commenter in the same state was offboarded and another says it effectively means offboarding, but one person was reactivated overnight.

topics.quote: I am getting no help from the project leads.
topics.summary: The poster gets no help from project leads, the status is left unclear rather than formally ended, and the only advice one person got was to post in Slack and keep logging in daily.

topics.quote: Hope to get a new instant offer soon for a new end client
topics.summary: A commenter who was offboarded is waiting for a new project offer.

topics.quote: Another rejection
topics.summary: The poster reports being rejected again, apparently after applying to Mercor.

topics.quote: When will LA go back to normal?
topics.summary: The poster is unhappy that the LA project now seems to offer only coding tasks and asks when it will return to normal.

topics.quote: Should I install insightful, login with SSO and start the timer as I read the docs and install the softwares?
topics.summary: The poster asks whether onboarding time for the Odin project can be billed and how to track it with the Insightful timer.

topics.quote: It is so bitterly confusing.
topics.summary: The poster finds the Odin onboarding confusing and unclear, and a commenter asks why a Mac (M-series) is needed for onboarding.

topics.quote: Not for everyone, apparently.
topics.summary: Commenters note the Odin project was paused for some people but not for others.

topics.quote: Submit first task, get 12 hours, complete 3 more tasks, get 3 more hours added for each.
topics.summary: The poster asks whether the 3-hour weekly cap rises, and a worker says it grows step by step to 60 hours in production and 80 hours for Super Writers.

topics.quote: I started out at 40/hr as trial, then 55/hr at production, now im at 75/hr as super writer.
topics.summary: The poster was offered $60/hr, and a worker reports their rate rising from $40 in trial to $55 in production and $75 as a Super Writer.

topics.quote: I am balling my eyes out now... I just can't seem to get in.
topics.summary: One person says they can't get onto the project, and another claims many people are hired knowing most won't make it through.
